title: Cut mute, high F endings and playing first trumpet
summary: Discussion of the cut mute, how arrangers wrote high F endings for the trumpets, and who hit the high F on the Shine record.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: This is the interlude I've seen you while. Like that. How do you get that tone? It's a mute. We call it a cut mute. I can hear that you're leaning a second. That's all I used to do, play a voice with different people. Did they write a lot of hard stuff for first in those days? Man, they had all the hard work. Just write down F for all of them. Bands were writing like that then. They would write F.
They would write a lot of hard work. They would write a lot of hard work. That's F above the stand.
That's right. For endings, you know.
I got some records, old records with Orr used to make F on.

I think it was the record Shine, I thought. Made F on the floor. Did Orr make the F? No, me. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. No, Orr didn't have too high a range on his horn when he was... Big broad sound, you know. What's on the other side?
